text.tspan: WAIT future — drains the shared ReadyQueue
(token, is_write) pairs pushed by per-channel ChannelWakers
translated back to ids via token_to_id
Pass 1 (sequential): connect + read the ready ids
plaintext drains the socket in a tight try_read loop
SSL keeps the async fallback (rustls owns the I/O state)

g.text: Pass 2 (concurrent): write the same set of channels

text.tspan: re-arm: every id in interest_dirty is armed again
(a missed arm is a data stall — when in doubt, mark dirty)

g.text: return completed sends + receives + disconnected channels

div.p: FxHashMap / FxHashSet keyed by Arc<str> connection id — SipHash was ~10% of CPU in a TLS profile.

text.tspan: scratch state is a field, not future-local,
so a cancelled WAIT loses nothing
